note: Track intervals, mix step 7 (all twelve, down and together): three ear games, each changing one thing: all twelve falling, all twelve with both notes at once ("level": "advanced" with "dir"), then the three close ones narrowed with "set". Folds in the all-twelve-falling drill, whose hum-back check is the first section's fix. Missing: interval-ears has no "dir" that mixes directions from one question to the next.

exercise.title: All twelve intervals, down and together
exercise.why: Two notes sounded together give you no first note to count from, so naming all twelve that way makes you hear each interval as one sound.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below to hear two notes, the upper one first: any of the twelve intervals up to an octave. Pick the interval's name.
If two answers sound alike, press Replay in the game and hum the two notes from the lower one up.
Practice until the 7ths and the tritone come as quickly as the 5th.

Press Start in the game below to hear the same twelve, with both notes at once.
Listen for the lower note first, then for how far over it the upper one sits.
When the two notes come together, the order is gone but each interval keeps its size.

Press Start in the game below to hear only three intervals, both notes at once. Pick P4 for a 4th, TT for the tritone or P5 for a 5th.
The three are a half step apart in size, so find the one in the middle, TT, and place the other two under and over it.
Practice until the three no longer sound alike.
